Setup

Quick Start
ApproachCommand / Code
Play CDN (dev)<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
NPM installnpm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli
CSS entry@import "tailwindcss";
Buildnpx @tailwindcss/cli -i input.css -o output.css --watch
v4 Change: No tailwind.config.js needed by default. Configuration is CSS-first using @theme. The old PostCSS config is optional.
BS â†’ TW: Bootstrap drops CSS + JS via <link>. Tailwind is pure CSS â€” no JS needed for components. Addiclick interactivity yourself (or use Alpine, HTMX, etc.).

Core Concepts

Utility-First vs Component Classes

Bootstrap gives you pre-built components (.card, .navbar). Tailwind gives you primitive utilities you compose together.

<!-- Bootstrap -->
<div class="card shadow-sm">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Card</h5>
    <p class="card-text">Content</p>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Tailwind â€” same result, built from utilities -->
<div class="bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden">
  <div class="p-6">
    <h2 class="text-xl font-semibold text-gray-900">Card</h2>
    <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600">Content</p>
  </div>
</div>
Mindset shift: Instead of searching for "the right BS class", you compose tiny single-purpose classes. .card (1 class) â†’ bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden (4 classes).
Responsive & State Variants

Like Bootstrap's breakpoint prefixes (.col-md-6), Tailwind uses prefixes on any utility:

<!-- Bootstrap -->
<div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-4">...</div>

<!-- Tailwind -->
<div class="w-full md:w-1/2 lg:w-1/3">...</div>

<!-- State variants work on ANY class -->
<button class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 focus:ring-2
               active:scale-95 disabled:opacity-50">
  Click
</button>

<!-- Group hover (BS doesn't have this) -->
<div class="group">
  <h3 class="group-hover:text-blue-600">Title</h3>
</div>
Key difference: In BS, hover: only works on some components. In Tailwind, every utility gets every variant: sm:md:lg:xl:2xl:, hover:focus:active:visited:disabled:, dark:print:portrait:landscape:, group-hover:peer-checked:, and custom ones via @custom-variant.

Layout

Grid System

Bootstrap's 12-column grid becomes Tailwind's grid-cols-*:

<!-- Bootstrap: 3 equal columns with gap -->
<div class="container">
  <div class="row g-4">
    <div class="col-md-4">Column 1</div>
    <div class="col-md-4">Column 2</div>
    <div class="col-md-4">Column 3</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Tailwind: same layout -->
<div class="container mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4">
  <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
    <div>Column 1</div>
    <div>Column 2</div>
    <div>Column 3</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Mixed column widths (12-col style) -->
<div class="grid grid-cols-12 gap-4">
  <div class="col-span-12 md:col-span-8">Main</div>
  <div class="col-span-12 md:col-span-4">Sidebar</div>
</div>
Flexbox alternative: flex flex-wrap gap-4 with w-1/3 works too â€” more like BS row/col.
BS â†’ TW: .container = container mx-auto max-w-7xl (or max-w-6xl). .row = grid grid-cols-12 gap-4 (or flex flex-wrap). .col-md-4 = md:col-span-4.
Container & Sizing
<!-- Containers -->
<div class="container mx-auto px-4 max-w-7xl">Full container</div>
<div class="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4">Narrow content</div>
<div class="w-full">Fluid (container-fluid)</div>

<!-- Width / Height -->
.w-full / .w-1/2 / .w-1/3 / .w-3/4
.max-w-md / .max-w-lg / .max-w-3xl / .max-w-7xl
.h-full / .h-screen / .h-64 / .min-h-screen

<!-- Arbitrary values -->
.w-[420px] / .h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] / .max-w-[900px]

Heading & Text Scale
BootstrapTailwind

<!-- Bold -->
.font-thin (100) / .font-light (300) / .font-normal (400)
.font-medium (500) / .font-semibold (600)
.font-bold (700) / .font-extrabold (800) / .font-black (900)

<!-- Extra utilities BS doesn't have -->
.tracking-tight / .tracking-wide    /* letter-spacing */
.leading-tight / .leading-relaxed   /* line-height */
.truncate                           /* text-truncate */
.line-clamp-2                       /* clamp to 2 lines */
.whitespace-nowrap                  /* text-nowrap */
.antialiased                        /* font-smoothing */

Spacing & Sizing

Margin, Padding, Gap

Good news: Tailwind uses the same scale as Bootstrap (0â€“5 = 0â€“3rem).

<!-- Identical syntax -->
.m-0 / .m-1 / .m-2 / .m-3 / .m-4 / .m-5    /* 0â€“3rem */
.p-0 / .p-1 / .p-2 / .p-3 / .p-4 / .p-5
.mt- / .mb- / .ml- / .mr- / .pt- / .pb- / .pl- / .pr-

<!-- EXCEPT Tailwind uses 's' not 's' for start/end -->
.ps-3 = .pl-3 (or .ms-3 for margin-inline-start)
.pe-3 = .pr-3
.ms-auto                              /* margin-left: auto */
.mx-auto                              /* center block */

<!-- Gap (same as BS .g-*) -->
.gap-2 / .gap-4 / .gap-x-6 / .gap-y-8

<!-- Space between children (BS doesn't have) -->
.space-y-4 / .space-x-4

<!-- Extra values BS doesn't have -->
.p-6 (1.5rem) / .p-8 (2rem) / .p-10 (2.5rem) / .p-12 (3rem)
.p-16 (4rem) / .p-20 (5rem) / .p-24 (6rem)

<!-- Arbitrary -->
.p-[17px] / .mt-[calc(100vh-80px)]
BS â†’ TW: The spacing scale 0â€“5 is identical. Tailwind adds 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 72, 80, 96. So .mt-3 works in both â€” you already know it.

Colors & Backgrounds

Tailwind Color Palette

Bootstrap has 8 named colors (primary, secondary, success, danger, warning, info, light, dark). Tailwind has 22 color families, each with 10â€“11 shades (50â€“950).

<!-- Text -->
.text-gray-500 / .text-blue-600 / .text-red-500
.text-emerald-400 / .text-violet-600 / .text-amber-500
.text-rose-600 / .text-teal-500 / .text-sky-400
.hover:text-blue-700 / .dark:text-white

<!-- Background -->
.bg-gray-100 / .bg-blue-50 / .bg-red-600
.bg-gradient-to-r from-cyan-500 to-blue-600
.bg-gradient-to-br from-purple-600 to-pink-500

<!-- Opacity modifiers -->
.bg-black/50        /* 50% opacity black */
.text-white/80      /* 80% opacity white */
.bg-blue-500/20     /* 20% opacity blue-500 */
.hover:bg-black/10  /* 10% on hover */

<!-- BS color mapping -->
.text-primary  â†’ text-blue-600
.text-danger   â†’ text-red-600
.text-success  â†’ text-green-600
.text-warning  â†’ text-yellow-500
.text-info     â†’ text-cyan-500
.text-dark     â†’ text-gray-900
.text-light    â†’ text-gray-100
Ring (BS doesn't have this)

Tailwind's ring utilities replace focus outlines:

<!-- Focus ring (like Bootstrap's :focus but better) -->
.focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2

<!-- Always-visible ring (BS has no equivalent) -->
.ring-2 ring-blue-500 ring-offset-2 ring-offset-gray-100

Borders, Shadows & Rings

Borders
<!-- Same concept, more control -->

.border-t-4 border-emerald-400
.border-b border-dashed border-gray-300

<!-- Radius -->

.rounded-sm    â†’ .rounded-1
.rounded       â†’ .rounded-2

.rounded-2xl   â†’ (no BS equivalent, 1rem)
.rounded-3xl   â†’ (no BS equivalent, 1.5rem)

Same naming but more options:

.shadow-sm    â†’ .shadow-sm        /* identical */
.shadow       â†’ .shadow           /* BS = TW shadow-md-ish */
.shadow-lg    â†’ .shadow-lg        /* identical */
.shadow-md    â†’ (BS has no .shadow-md)
.shadow-xl    â†’ (BS has no .shadow-xl)
.shadow-2xl   â†’ (BS has no .shadow-2xl)
.shadow-inner â†’ (BS has no .shadow-inner)
sm default md lg xl 2xl

Effects & Animation

Transitions & Transforms

This is where Tailwind massively outshines Bootstrap. BS has no built-in transition/transform utilities.

<!-- Transition (BS has NO equivalent) -->
<button class="transition-all duration-300 ease-in-out
               hover:scale-105 hover:shadow-lg
               active:scale-95">
  Smooth hover
</button>

<!-- Animation utilities -->
.animate-spin          /* rotate 360Â° */
.animate-ping          /* radar ping */
.animate-pulse         /* fade pulse */
.animate-bounce        /* bounce */
.animate-none

<!-- Opacity -->
.opacity-0 â†’ .invisible (hidden)
.opacity-50 / .opacity-100
.hover:opacity-80

<!-- Filters -->
.blur-sm / .blur-lg / .grayscale / .brightness-110
.contrast-125 / .drop-shadow-lg / .sepia
.hover:saturate-150

<!-- Backdrop filters (glassmorphism) -->
.backdrop-blur-sm / .backdrop-blur-lg
.backdrop-brightness-50

Forms & Inputs

Styled Form Controls

Bootstrap's .form-control = a composed set of Tailwind utilities:

<!-- Bootstrap .form-control -->
<input class="form-control" placeholder="Name">

<!-- Tailwind equivalent -->
<input class="w-full px-3 py-2 border border-gray-300
       rounded-lg shadow-sm
       focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500
       focus:border-transparent
       placeholder:text-gray-400" placeholder="Name">

<!-- Select -->
<select class="w-full px-3 py-2 border border-gray-300
              rounded-lg bg-white">
  <option>Option</option>
</select>

<!-- Checkbox -->
<label class="flex items-center gap-2">
  <input type="checkbox" class="h-4 w-4 text-blue-600
         border-gray-300 rounded focus:ring-blue-500">
  <span class="text-sm text-gray-700">Remember me</span>
</label>

<!-- Switch toggle (native) -->
<label class="relative inline-flex items-center cursor-pointer">
  <input type="checkbox" class="sr-only peer">
  <div class="w-9 h-5 bg-gray-200 peer-checked:bg-blue-600
              rounded-full peer-focus:ring-2 peer-focus:ring-blue-300
              after:content-[''] after:absolute after:top-0.5
              after:left-0.5 after:bg-white after:rounded-full
              after:h-4 after:w-4 after:transition-all
              peer-checked:after:translate-x-4"></div>
  <span class="ml-2 text-sm">Toggle</span>
</label>

<!-- Input group -->
<div class="flex">
  <span class="inline-flex items-center px-3 bg-gray-100
               border border-r-0 border-gray-300 rounded-l-lg">
    @
  </span>
  <input class="flex-1 px-3 py-2 border border-gray-300
               rounded-r-lg focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500
               focus:outline-none" placeholder="Username">
</div>
BS â†’ TW: Bootstrap's .form-control handles focus, border, padding in one class. Tailwind makes you compose 5â€“7 utilities â€” but you get total control over every detail (focus ring color, border radius per side, placeholder styling).

Dark Mode

Dark Variant

Bootstrap uses data-bs-theme="dark". Tailwind uses the dark: prefix with a class on <html>.

<!-- Bootstrap -->
<html data-bs-theme="dark">
<div class="bg-dark text-light">Dark section</div>

<!-- Tailwind -->
<html class="dark">
<div class="bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 dark:bg-black dark:text-white">
  Dark section
</div>

<!-- Every utility can be toggled -->
<div class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-800
            text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-100
            border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700
            shadow-md dark:shadow-none">
  Theme-aware card
</div>

<!-- JS toggle -->
document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark');
localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
Key difference: BS's dark mode is opt-in per component (data-bs-theme overrides). Tailwind's dark: lets you toggle individual properties â€” much finer control.

Customization

CSS-First Config via @theme (v4)

Bootstrap uses --bs-* CSS vars or SASS. Tailwind v4 uses the @theme directive â€” no config file needed.

@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  /* Colors â€” like --bs-primary */
  --color-primary: #ff6600;
  --color-primary-dark: #cc5200;

  /* Spacing â€” extend the scale */
  --spacing-18: 4.5rem;

  /* Fonts */
  --font-family-display: 'Cinzel', serif;

  /* Border radius */
  --radius-4xl: 2rem;

  /* Shadows */
  --shadow-glow: 0 0 20px rgba(255, 102, 0, 0.3);

  /* Breakpoints */
  --breakpoint-3xl: 2000px;
}

/* Then use anywhere: bg-primary, font-display, shadow-glow */
@apply & Layers (like BS component classes)

Use @apply to create Bootstrap-style component classes from utilities:

@layer components {
  .btn-primary {
    @apply inline-flex items-center px-4 py-2
           bg-blue-600 text-white font-medium text-sm
           rounded-lg hover:bg-blue-700
           transition-colors duration-200;
  }

  .card-bs {
    @apply bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden;
  }

  .card-body {
    @apply p-6;
  }
}

@layer base {
  h1 { @apply text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight; }
  body { @apply antialiased text-gray-900; }
}

@layer utilities {
  .text-balance { text-wrap: balance; }
}
BS â†’ TW: BS gives you .btn-primary out of the box. Tailwind makes you define it yourself via @apply. More work upfront, but you control everything â€” no "Bootstrap look" limitation.

Common Patterns

Card with Header + Footer
<div class="bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden">
  <div class="px-6 py-4 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50">
    <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900">Header</h3>
  </div>
  <div class="p-6">
    <p class="text-gray-600">Body content here.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="px-6 py-4 border-t border-gray-200 bg-gray-50
              flex items-center justify-end gap-2">
    <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm rounded-lg
                   bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700">
      Save
    </button>
  </div>
</div>
Compare to BS: .card â†’ bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden. Same visual, you just write the primitives.
Navbar (Dark)
<nav class="flex items-center justify-between px-4 py-3
            bg-gray-900 text-white">
  <a href="#" class="text-xl font-bold">Brand</a>

  <!-- Desktop nav -->
  <div class="hidden md:flex items-center gap-4">
    <a href="#" class="px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium
                       rounded-lg hover:bg-gray-800">Home</a>
    <a href="#" class="px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium
                       rounded-lg hover:bg-gray-800">About</a>
  </div>

  <!-- Mobile hamburger -->
  <button class="md:hidden p-2 rounded-lg hover:bg-gray-800">
    <svg class="w-6 h-6" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24"
         stroke="currentColor">
      <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2"
            d="M4 6h16M4 12h16M4 18h16"/>
    </svg>
  </button>
</nav>
Modal Dialog
<!-- Backdrop -->
<div class="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 z-40"></div>

<!-- Modal -->
<div class="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center p-4">
  <div class="bg-white rounded-xl shadow-2xl w-full max-w-lg">

    <!-- Header -->
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4
                border-b border-gray-200">
      <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold">Modal Title</h3>
      <button class="text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600 text-2xl
                     leading-none">×</button>
    </div>

    <!-- Body -->
    <div class="px-6 py-4">
      <p class="text-gray-600">Content here.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Footer -->
    <div class="flex items-center justify-end gap-2 px-6 py-4
                border-t border-gray-200">
      <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm rounded-lg
                     border border-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50">
        Cancel
      </button>
      <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm rounded-lg
                     bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700">
        Confirm
      </button>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
Note: BS handles modal open/close with JS. Tailwind just toggles hidden / fixed classes â€” you need your own JS or a library like Alpine.js.

<div class="relative px-4 py-3 rounded-lg

<!-- Color variants -->
.bg-blue-100 text-blue-800 border-blue-200  /* primary */

Responsive Design

<!-- Bootstrap responsive layout -->
<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-8">Main</div>
    <div class="col-12 col-md-4">Sidebar</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Tailwind responsive layout -->
<div class="container mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4">
  <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-12 gap-6">
    <main class="md:col-span-8">Main</main>
    <aside class="md:col-span-4">Sidebar</aside>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Responsive text + spacing -->
<div class="p-4 md:p-8 text-sm md:text-base lg:text-lg
            text-center md:text-left">
  Responsive padding, font-size, alignment
</div>

<!-- Responsive visibility (like d-none d-md-block) -->
<div class="hidden md:block">Visible on md+</div>
<div class="block md:hidden">Visible on mobile only</div>
